items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: I think they called him Busby Berkeley, and he was not a dancer, but he had Mr. Buddy Bradley doing the choreographies for those dance numbers in the movies

ctx.x: first of 1931, in February. See, because people like George M. Cohen -- by the way, James Cagney was teaching on the third floor also. He was a dance teacher in the Billy Pierce Studio, and he had students like Dan Dailey, Van Johnson, even James Stewart, he used to come there, see. And they -- they became very famous in moving pictures, you see, these people, which also happened to Eleanor Powell and Arlene Judge, Rita Hayworth, Lucille Ball, Joan Blondell -- she used to come there -- and Nancy Carroll, she was…

And I think a friend of mine, Mr. Buddy Bradley's wife, you know, widow, Lady B. Bradley, she explained to me about Clifton Webb, you see. He was also a student of Buddy Bradley, and he was very popular. You know, George M. Cohen, he was a very popular man, famous for composing songs, putting on Broadway shows and all this, and that's really what Mr. Buddy Bradley was involved in at the time he left for England, because he was doing the choreographies for these great shows, these Broadway shows, and they weren't…
